claims.text: The degree of local chemical ordering governs the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Atomic size mismatch modulates local chemical ordering in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Local chemical ordering influences vacancy formation energies.
Local chemical ordering influences atomic diffusion barriers.
The proposed nanoalloys contain an equiatomic or near-equiatomic distribution of 5–7 principal elements.
Atomic size mismatch drives local chemical ordering that creates spatially varying vacancy formation energies.
Atomic size mismatch drives local chemical ordering that creates spatially varying diffusion barriers.
Local chemical ordering arising from significant atomic size mismatch increases vacancy formation energies.
Local chemical ordering arising from significant atomic size mismatch reduces atomic diffusion.
Increasing vacancy formation energies and reducing diffusion stabilize the lattice.
Engineered, locally ordered nanoalloys will have higher vacancy formation energies than randomly mixed nanoalloys.
Engineered, locally ordered nanoalloys will have lower atomic diffusion rates than randomly mixed nanoalloys.
Engineered, locally ordered nanoalloys will have greater structural and chemical stability than randomly mixed nanoalloys.
The prediction is limited to application-specific high-temperature conditions and compositions containing 5–7 principal elements.

A lack of statistically significant increases in vacancy formation energy, decreases in diffusion rate, and improved structural stability in the engineered alloys relative to random controls would falsify the hypothesis.
